title: DMK MLA GV Markandeyan Arrested Over Threatening Remarks Against Tamil Nadu CM Vijay
excerpt: The Vilathikulam legislator was detained by police after allegedly making threatening and controversial remarks against Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay at a public meeting in Kovilpatti, marking the second arrest of a DMK MLA over anti-Vijay remarks in recent weeks.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • DMK MLA GV Markandeyan was arrested for threatening remarks against Tamil Nadu CM C. Joseph Vijay.
  • DMK leaders condemned the arrest, alleging systematic targeting of opposition by the TVK-led government.
  • Markandeyan's arrest follows another DMK MLA's detention for similar remarks just weeks earlier.
  • The arrests highlight escalating tensions between the ruling TVK and opposition DMK in Tamil Nadu.
Political Tensions Escalate in Tamil Nadu
›GV Markandeyan arrested on July 20 for threatening remarks.
›Second DMK MLA arrested in weeks over anti-CM comments.
›Protests erupted following Markandeyan's arrest near police station.
›DMK accuses TVK government of political vendetta.
Source: The Hindu
  • DMK MLA GV Markandeyan, representing Vilathikulam in Thoothukudi district, was arrested on July 20 for allegedly threatening Tamil Nadu CM C. Joseph Vijay during a public meeting in Kovilpatti.
  • DMK chief MK Stalin and senior leader Kanimozhi condemned the arrest, accusing the TVK-led government of systematically targeting opposition leaders.
  • This marks the second arrest of a DMK legislator over remarks against CM Vijay in recent weeks, after former minister Anitha R. Radhakrishnan was detained in a similar case in early July.
  • The arrest escalates the intensifying political confrontation between the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) and the opposition DMK ahead of crucial political battles in the state.

Tamil Nadu police arrested DMK MLA GV Markandeyan on Sunday after he allegedly made threatening and controversial remarks against Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay during a public meeting in Kovilpatti, according to multiple reports. Markandeyan represents the Vilathikulam constituency in Thoothukudi district.

Police detained the legislator, questioned him, and said they planned to produce him before a magistrate. The arrest triggered immediate protests from Markandeyan's supporters near the police station, adding to the charged political atmosphere in the state's southern districts.

DMK Leaders Condemn Arrest

DMK president MK Stalin and senior party leader Kanimozhi swiftly condemned the arrest, accusing the TVK-led state government of using law enforcement to silence and target opposition leaders, according to The Hindu. The DMK has framed the action as part of a broader pattern of political vendetta by the Vijay-led administration.

"This government is systematically going after DMK leaders who dare to criticise the chief minister," the party said in a statement, demanding Markandeyan's immediate release.

Second DMK MLA Arrested in Weeks

Markandeyan's arrest comes barely weeks after another DMK legislator, former minister Anitha R. Radhakrishnan, was arrested in Thoothukudi district on similar charges. Radhakrishnan, the Tiruchendur MLA, was taken into custody after the Madras High Court rejected his anticipatory bail plea in a case stemming from a speech he delivered at a DMK public meeting on June 20.

In that case, police registered an FIR under Sections 352 and 353 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita — relating to intentional insult and promoting enmity — after Radhakrishnan allegedly made derogatory remarks targeting CM Vijay, including comments linked to a birthday photograph shared by actor Trisha featuring the chief minister. He was later granted bail.

Deepening TVK-DMK Tensions

The arrests form part of a broader and intensifying political confrontation between Vijay's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), which swept to power in the 2026 Tamil Nadu assembly elections, and the DMK, now the principal opposition. The rivalry has spilled beyond the legislature into police stations and courtrooms.

In recent weeks, the two parties have traded accusations over attempts to poach each other's legislators. Police arrested three individuals accused of offering ₹35 crore to a TVK lawmaker to vote against the assembly speaker, while the DMK has demanded a vigilance inquiry into what it calls poaching attempts by the chief minister's camp.

Separately, the DMK has sought a CBI investigation into CM Vijay's public remarks on the Karur stampede that occurred during one of his political campaign events, alleging that his statements amounted to influencing witnesses.

A Legislator Who Switched Sides

Markandeyan, originally elected as an AIADMK MLA from Vilathikulam in 2011, was expelled from the party after contesting as an independent rebel in the 2019 by-election. He subsequently joined the DMK and won the seat again in the 2021 assembly elections and retained it in the 2026 polls, narrowly defeating TVK's P. Kasiram.

The arrest is likely to further polarise an already volatile political landscape in Tamil Nadu, where Vijay's transition from one of the state's biggest film stars to chief minister has created new political fault lines and tested the boundaries of political speech against the head of government.
